title: EMEA Data Center Outlook: 5 Things To Know | BloombergNEF
gist: BNEF's base case sees EMEA data-center capacity rising 2.5x from 19.2GW (1Q 2026) to 53.1GW by 2035, led by the UK and Germany, with Spain and Finland rising and grid-constrained Ireland and the Netherlands falling out of the top five. The EU will miss its CADA goal to triple computing capacity by 2030 (16.3GW vs an implied 27.4GW), AI training is a much smaller share in EMEA (5%) than the US (14%), and grid-connection rules and first-time developers are key execution risks.

insights.claim: BNEF's base case has EMEA data-center power capacity reaching 53.1GW by 2035, up from an estimated 19.2GW in 1Q 2026 (about 2.5x).
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: Sustained multi-year demand growth for power, grid equipment and data-center infrastructure across EMEA.

insights.claim: The UK (7.7GW) and Germany (5.1GW) are projected to remain EMEA's largest data-center markets in 2035.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: UK and German power/grid and data-center landlords capture the largest share of EMEA build-out.

insights.claim: Spain and Finland climb the EMEA data-center rankings as early-stage projects come online toward the end of the decade, while ongoing constraints push Ireland and the Netherlands out of the top five.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: Growth is migrating from constrained legacy hubs to power-rich newer markets; site/grid exposure in Spain and Finland gains relevance.

insights.claim: Average EMEA data-center power draw in 2035 is estimated at 28GW, well below the 53.1GW peak figure (which assumes max server utilization on the hottest day), equating to 246TWh of annual energy demand.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: Use ~28GW average / 246TWh, not nameplate peak, when sizing power-demand upside for European utilities and generators.
insights.locator: Data centers will draw significantly less

insights.claim: Peak data-center capacity figures overstate actual electricity consumption because they assume all servers run at maximum utilization on the hottest day of the year.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: Distinguish peak capacity (grid connection sizing) from average draw (energy sales) when modeling utility revenue impact.
insights.locator: Data centers will draw significantly less

insights.claim: The EU's Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) aims to triple data-center computing capacity from 2026 levels by 2030, part of a wider proposed framework to accelerate digital infrastructure.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: Policy tailwind for EU data-center permitting and investment.

insights.claim: BNEF projects EU IT capacity growing from 9.1GW at end-2026 to 16.3GW in 2030, well short of the implied 27.4GW CADA target, so the target is likely to be missed.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: Expect a policy-vs-pipeline gap that may trigger further EU support measures or faster grid-connection reforms.
insights.locator: This target is likely to be missed

insights.claim: BNEF estimates EU IT capacity reaches 26.4GW by 2035, slightly short of the tripling goal, and a little growth in the project pipeline would reach it — making the goal achievable on a longer timeline.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: EU data-center build-out is delayed rather than capped; long-duration investors can underwrite growth beyond 2030.
insights.locator: The EU does not directly state

themes.theme: AI training demand gap: US vs EMEA

insights.claim: About 14% of US data-center capacity is likely to serve AI training in 2035, versus just 5% in EMEA, per BNEF modelling.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: AI-training-driven power demand upside is concentrated in the US; EMEA demand is more cloud/inference-driven.
insights.locator: 3. AI training plays a bigger role

insights.claim: AI model development is dominated by the US and China, companies typically use compute capacity near home, and European AI companies make up less than 1% of total revenue tracked by BNEF — explaining EMEA's lower AI-training share.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: Absence of European frontier AI labs limits Europe's share of the highest-intensity data-center demand.
insights.quote: European AI companies make up less than 1% of total revenue tracked by BNEF.

insights.claim: European markets are slimming down grid-connection rules for data centers in response to heavy grid strain, with France and the UK in particular accelerating connection processes, driven by digital sovereignty priorities.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: France and the UK become relatively advantaged locations for faster data-center energization.

insights.claim: Because data centers out-competing traditional industry for power may be politically untenable, Spain and Denmark are considering rules that would help other industries access power capacity.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: Political pushback could constrain data-center grid access in Spain despite its rising pipeline — a risk to its growth outlook.
insights.quote: But data centers out-competing traditional industry might be politically untenable

insights.claim: The grid-connection rules ultimately adopted by European governments could have a big impact on which markets realize their data-center growth prospects.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: Track national grid-connection reforms as a leading indicator for country-level data-center winners.

insights.claim: First-time developers make up a smaller share of the European data-center pipeline than in the US, but that share is climbing.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: A growing share of speculative pipeline implies headline pipeline figures overstate deliverable capacity.
insights.locator: 5. First-timers make up a smaller share

insights.claim: Projects from first-time data-center developers are at greater risk of delays or cancellation, with execution risk particularly acute for teams lacking prior delivery experience.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: Haircut pipeline estimates for inexperienced sponsors; experienced operators have a relative advantage.

insights.claim: In Europe, first-time developer activity is most extreme in the UK and Spain, where they are proposing many early-stage projects that have not yet secured development permits.
insights.speaker: ajacob84
insights.so_what: UK and Spain pipeline headlines carry higher cancellation risk than they appear.
insights.locator: Within Europe, this is most extreme
